newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge orders Liggett to deliver documents.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge orders Liggett to deliver documents.

text.p: A Florida judge on Wednesday ordered Liggett Group to immediately deliver internal documents for possible use in the state of Florida's lawsuit against cigarette companies.

Courts in Texas and Illinois have issued similar orders since Thursday, when Liggett Group, the nation's fifth largest cigarette maker, which is owned by Brooke Group, struck a sweeping deal with 22 states suing the tobacco industry for an estimated $30 billion spent on sick smokers.
Judge Harold Cohen of Palm Beach County Circuit Court also ordered an accelerated review of about 20 Liggett documents that attorneys for the state claim affect public safety.
Cohen assigned William Rutter, a retired judge aiding in the pre-trial screening of documents, to review the 20 Liggett documents and to make a recommendation to him within 10 days.
A hearing on that recommendation will be held April 14, Cohen said.
Under Florida law, trade-secret protections and client-lawyer privilege, which ordinarily safeguard internal documents, can be overriden if matters of public safety are at stake.
Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth told reporters that the 20 documents, which he said he had not seen, would be made public if the judge agrees that public health was at issue.
Cohen has scheduled an Aug. 4 start for the jury trial on the Florida lawsuit, the second after Mississippi's expected to come to trial.

Florida is claiming at least $1 billion for tobacco-related Medicare spending and has won the right to pursue much higher awards if the tobacco companies are found to have operated as racketeers under a state conspiracy law.
The tobacco companies deny any conspiracy and claim the state itself had produced cigarettes for prison inmates and benefitted in many other ways from their businesses.
